items.title: Citi and PNC join banks making customers liable for what AI agents do with their logins
items.summary: Customers who give outside agents their logins carry the risk, even after a hack. ChatGPT Wallet pays with a network token instead.
items.content_html:
Customers who give outside agents their logins carry the risk, even after a hack. ChatGPT Wallet pays with a network token instead.

  • Citi changed its online user agreement this week: customers are responsible for what third-party AI agents do with their credentials, even if the tool is hacked. Citi's own agents add no such liability
  • Nov 18 PNC changed its terms. JPMorgan and Bank of America adopted similar policies in October, and Citizens emailed customers a warning
  • US Pro ChatGPT Wallet is open to Pro subscribers in the US. It pays through the major card networks with a token in place of the card number, and every purchase needs a security check such as Face ID
  • JPMorgan blocks agents that shop with a card number a customer hands them, the WSJ reported. Its payments arm is now in Visa's Agentic Ready program, which has 140-plus members

Autopilot, an always-on agent with its own ID and a named manager, starts rolling out. No prices yet.

  • 50M+ agents in Agent 365, Microsoft's control plane for governing them
  • Autopilot an always-on agent with its own Entra Agent ID and a named manager, now rolling out to customers in Microsoft's Frontier early-access program
  • ~80% of Fortune 500 companies use Cowork, Microsoft says
  • 40% more tokens per watt Microsoft says its new Maia 300 chip will deliver than leading GPU-based systems

Sources:

  1. Microsoft: Nadella's Ignite keynote, edited (Company)
  2. Microsoft Copilot: Autopilot, Office and Cowork details (Company)

items.title: Employers blamed AI for 1 in 5 US job cuts this year, but under 3% in October
items.summary: Goldman expects a low-hire, low-fire market for another year, with AI displacement growing later.
items.content_html:
Goldman expects a low-hire, low-fire market for another year, with AI displacement growing later.

  • 121,401 announced US job cuts cited AI through October, about 20% of 617,189 (Challenger)
  • 1,265 cuts cited AI in October, under 3% of the month, against about 40% in May
  • Up to 9% of workers could be displaced during the AI transition, Goldman economist Joseph Briggs estimated
  • 1% of payrolls laid off in September, or 1.6 million layoffs, while hires ran at 5.4 million (JOLTS)

Sources:

  1. HCA Magazine: Challenger's count through October (Press)
  2. TechJack: May and October shares (Press)
  3. Fortune: Goldman's 2027 outlook and JOLTS data (Press)
  4. People Managing People: The 22% share, through August (Press)

Confidence: Press + data
